Veterinary Visit Report

I took my cat for a check-up because I had noticed sores in his mouth, on the back, between his last teeth, and he was also losing weight.

The veterinarian examined him and said there were no oral changes besides a little tartar. However, she stated that he was experiencing a lot of pain in his back, near his tail—an area he never liked being touched. Despite this, he continued to climb on things normally and without difficulty.

Even so, gabapentin was prescribed, which made my cat extremely drowsy, but he remained unwell.

Blood tests and an ultrasound were ordered, which came back normal considering his age of 13 years. Later, a stool sample was taken, which also came back normal, along with an X-ray and another blood test to evaluate his thyroid, since he has had hyperthyroidism for 5 years.

When I received the thyroid test results, I realized that the test had been ordered for hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism. I sent the results to the veterinarian and pointed out the error. Initially, she reviewed the test and said it was normal and that there was no error. After I insisted and explained the problem, she finally acknowledged the mistake and said she would order a repeat test.

The endocrinologist was also involved in the situation and, instead of properly clarifying what happened, informed me that the result would be exactly the same value and that only the "header" of the test would change. They said the test would be redone, but, given everything that happened, I doubt it was actually redone.

I had one more appointment after this episode, but I decided I will not return to that place.

During all these years of monitoring my cat's hyperthyroidism, the test ordered to evaluate the thyroid is done by chemiluminescence, assessing T4 and TSH. Therefore, I consider it even more serious that they requested a test to investigate hypothyroidism.

Finally, I found a veterinarian specializing in veterinary dentistry, who identified precisely the wounds that I had already noticed in his mouth and that the veterinarian at Vet Care had not identified. He is already undergoing treatment and is showing improvement.

Disrespectful handling of appointments / poor communication. I’m very disappointed with how Vetcare Clinic handled my orthopedics appointment. I originally had an appointment on March 2 with the Vetcare orthopedist, which was canceled and rescheduled for March 3 at 11:00 AM.

I rearranged my day and went to the clinic, only to be told immediately upon arrival that the orthopedist could not attend. The issue isn’t that something unexpected happened—it’s that no one informed me before I got there. A simple call or message would have saved me a wasted trip. Lack of respect for the client's time / terrible communication // I was very disappointed with how Vetcare handled my appointment with the orthopedist. I had an appointment scheduled for March 2nd, which was canceled and rescheduled for March 3rd at 11:00 AM. I rearranged my schedule to be able to attend.

Upon arriving at the clinic, I was immediately informed that the orthopedist could not attend. The problem isn't exactly that unforeseen events can happen—that can occur—but rather the fact that no one notified me beforehand. A simple call or message would have prevented me from wasting time and traveling unnecessarily.

I work and have commitments, just like any pet owner. In total, I lost more than an hour and a half going to the clinic and back, only to find out on-site that the appointment wouldn't take place.

This is disrespectful and not an acceptable way to manage scheduling and service. Vetcare urgently needs to improve its communication with clients (timely cancellation notices, advance notice of cancellations, and better internal organization). Unfortunately, based on my experience, I do not recommend them.

As pet owners, we also have jobs and responsibilities. I lost more than an hour and a half traveling to the clinic and back for an appointment that should never have been kept on the schedule.

This is disrespectful and not an acceptable way to run a clinic. Vetcare needs to improve scheduling and client communication (timely cancellation notices, confirmation messages, and better coordination).

My dog's eye was injured by a cat on November 13th. I took her to the Emergency Room immediately, around 9 PM. The veterinarian examined her and identified a corneal lesion.
I was prescribed Vigamox 3 times a day for 14 days, Mydriacyl 2 times a day for 7 days, and Dipyrone for pain, as well as a follow-up appointment after 14 days. I confirmed the follow-up appointment time, as I thought it was too long, and he confirmed that this was indeed the case. I asked about warning signs, and he advised me that if she didn't open her eye within 3 days, I should contact him by phone.
Although I don't understand anything about veterinary medicine, this course of action didn't seem appropriate to me, especially regarding the follow-up time and the lack of indication for an evaluation by a specialist.
My dog ​​was seen the following morning by another veterinarian, who immediately recommended an evaluation by an ophthalmologist.
Hours later, she was seen by the ophthalmologist, who identified a very serious injury, with iris exposure, a significant increase in intraocular pressure, and an indication for urgent surgery.
We are still trying to save the puppy's eye, but if we had followed the instructions received at the clinic, we wouldn't have had any chance.

I wrote to the clinic reporting what happened, and I received a phone call from someone in the administrative area. I asked to speak with a professional, and they suggested a time on a weekday at 12:30 pm, a time that is clearly difficult for anyone who works. I offered any day after 4 pm, but I received a confusing message via WhatsApp saying that the schedule was very full until the end of the year and asking me to send the documents relating to the appointments and surgeries.

It is unbelievable that a clinic that claims to be complete, with dozens of specialties, does not properly refer patients and treats such a serious event with such indifference.

Run away from this place.

My experiences with this clinic have always been good; the professionals are very attentive, especially nurse Luís and Dr. Ana Paula. Unfortunately, my dog ​​had a very serious illness and didn't survive, but Dr. Ana Paula spared no effort to help her.
Excellent service and a very nice space.
Two years ago, my dog ​​was cared for by them, and the service was top-notch. Both the doctors and the receptionists were incredibly kind and attentive. I am very grateful to the entire team!

Unfortunately, even after being a client for over 10 years, we received no consideration from the clinic owners after error after error they made with our pet of almost 12 years. After a check-up and follow-up appointment, it was indicated that Dino needed emergency surgery due to a urinary tract obstruction. The surgery was scheduled for the same day at 4 PM. The surgeon was 1 hour late and the anesthesiologist was 3 hours late. During those 3 hours, we waited in the reception area without any information, as it was an emergency surgery. The surgery started, obviously late, and after it finished, the doctor came down to say that everything had gone well and that they would bring him down in 30 minutes. By 8:40 PM, there was no one left in the reception area, and the on-call nurse who was supposed to bring him down did not. After an hour, we called to see if anyone would answer, and she answered, saying she would come down in 20 minutes, which turned into 30. To top it all off, they brought him and the post-surgical clothes, all wet with urine. Yes, they handed us a recently operated pet, completely soaked in urine… you don't need a diploma to know the risk of infection, at the very least. And, to finish, the on-call doctor thought it was appropriate to say that we could wash the clothes and dry them with a hairdryer, in addition to asking us to come back the next day at 8 am to pay for the (terrible) service, given that she didn't know how to charge us.

We went back and paid. We filed a complaint and asked to speak to the owner of the clinic, and we never heard back from her. Clearly, they forgot that the clinic is made up of clients and that these clients are part of our family.
We have been customers for over 10 years and the experience has always been very good. Everyone treats us with great care, attention, and competence.

I'm a pet mom and a Vet Care client since 2023. My cats have been seen by Flávia Braz and Gabriela for regular, scheduled appointments. But I've also gone there for emergencies, at night, had a cat hospitalized, and unfortunately, even lost a kitten at this clinic. What I want to say is that in all these interactions, my cats and I were treated with respect and, more than that, with great care, by everyone who assisted us at reception, the assistants, the veterinarians in the hospitalization unit, and even after the passing of my kitten. I recommend them.

Last Saturday, I took my 15-year-old cat to the VetCare clinic because he was sneezing and having difficulty breathing. The on-call veterinarian informed me that he would need to be hospitalized for monitoring.

On Sunday, an X-ray was performed to assess pneumonia, and a small accumulation of fluid in the pleura was identified. In the hospitalization report I received, the team stated that drainage had not been necessary, as it was a small amount.

Despite receiving intravenous antibiotics, my cat showed no improvement on Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday. During those days, I only received hospitalization reports, without any direct contact from Dr. Camila Vitorato to explain the clinical picture. Even after insisting, I only managed to speak with her on Tuesday, after much persistence.

I was treated in an extremely arrogant manner, being questioned about why I wanted to speak with her. I explained that my cat had been hospitalized since Saturday, without showing improvement, and that I needed to understand what was happening. At that point, she suggested switching the antibiotic to a capsule one and gave me the prescription.

On Wednesday, again with no improvement, I received an audio message from Dr. Camila informing me that she had only contacted the team's pulmonologist that day, which I consider completely absurd. My cat had been hospitalized since Saturday with an altered respiratory condition, but only four days later was a specialist contacted!

Furthermore, she requested new medications, including bronchodilators, to include in the treatment – ​​something that, in my view, should have been done from the beginning of the hospitalization. Even worse, Dr. Camila implied that he would remain hospitalized until Friday, awaiting the pulmonologist's schedule, who could only see him in person that day. In other words, in addition to the four days of hospitalization already completed, I would be forced to pay for two more days, while my cat continued to suffer. A true absurdity! My cat could have died by Friday, such was the negligence and lack of urgency with which they treated the case.

Another very serious issue was the cardiac check-up performed at VetCare. Despite being charged immediately at the time of the exam, I still haven't received the report and images. I've requested them twice at the clinic and still nothing.

Furthermore, during the hospitalization updates, I was informed that my cat hadn't defecated since Saturday. When I decided to take him out of VetCare on Wednesday, the first action taken by the new team now caring for him was to treat the constipation that was causing him great discomfort. A catheter with liquid was inserted to remove accumulated feces, a very basic procedure completely ignored by VetCare.

I was also informed that my cat was nauseous due to the abrupt change from intravenous to capsule antibiotics, something that was immediately reversed. With a new antibiotic and proper care, he finally showed improvement.

In short, my cat spent four days hospitalized at VetCare, costing R$ 4,000.00 for exams and hospitalization, only to return home in the same condition he arrived in. The service was negligent, unprepared, and focused solely on generating more expenses for the client, with unnecessary exams and poorly conducted treatments.

Dr. Camila Vitorato's attitude was unacceptable: arrogant, distant, and lacking commitment to my cat's well-being. No effort was made to alleviate the animal's basic discomfort, such as the evident constipation, and only after days of hospitalization was an essential specialist called in.

When I picked up my cat from the hospital, they had even changed his food to a special diet due to his overweight. And I was informed that he wasn't eating! Obviously, in a serious health situation, changing his food at that moment was totally inappropriate!!! If the cat was barely breathing, why even think about a special diet????? Surreal!!!

The experience was traumatic and infuriating. VetCare has shown itself to be completely unprepared and to have a conduct that prioritizes profits over the care of animals.

Amazing! Impeccable and attentive service on WhatsApp and also from the doctors. Patient, understanding of even the most fearful and skittish animals, they are caring, and I was very happy to have listened to my inner voice and sought a …
Dr. Renata is amazing! Both with my cat and my dog, the consultations are always detailed and caring ❤️ Always up-to-date and professional.
Excellent many years ago with the surgeon Dr. Andrei, an excellent veterinarian and his team as well, but 10 years ago my Shih Tzu Bono Vox had surgery for bladder stones and then castration.
My dog ​​came in on April 28th and didn't get better. I brought her back today, she had blood tests and an ultrasound, and we're waiting to be seen... it's a shame, it was a good clinic. …
